name: Cuneiform Writing
description: The earliest known writing system, using wedge-shaped marks on clay tablets. Enabled record-keeping, literature, and administration across Mesopotamian civilizations.

name: The Wheel
description: Solid wooden wheel used first for pottery, then adapted for chariots and carts. Revolutionized transport and warfare across Eurasia.

name: Bronze Metallurgy
description: Alloying copper with tin (or arsenic) to produce harder, more durable tools and weapons. Defined the Bronze Age across Eurasia.

name: Papyrus
description: Writing surface made from pressed reed strips, lighter and more portable than clay tablets. Enabled long literary and administrative texts.

name: Alphabet
description: The first true phonetic alphabet, consisting of 22 consonant letters. Ancestor of Greek, Latin, Hebrew, Arabic, and nearly all modern alphabets.

name: Qanat Irrigation
description: Underground aqueduct system tapping mountain aquifers to bring water to arid lowlands without evaporation loss. Still in use today.

name: Iron Smelting
description: Smelting and working iron ore into tools and weapons, harder and cheaper than bronze. Launched the Iron Age across Eurasia.

name: Concrete (Opus Caementicium)
description: Hydraulic concrete using volcanic ash (pozzolana), enabling aqueducts, domes, and harbors that endure for millennia.

name: Zero and Decimal System
description: The positional decimal numeral system including a symbol for zero. Basis of modern arithmetic, transmitted through Arabic scholars to medieval Europe.

name: Paper
description: Pressed plant-fiber writing material, later refined by Cai Lun (c. 105 CE). Transformed literacy, record-keeping, and printing worldwide.

name: Stirrup
description: Foot support allowing riders to stand and strike from horseback. Transformed cavalry warfare from China to Europe.

name: Gunpowder
description: Black powder (saltpeter, sulfur, charcoal), first used in fireworks and fire arrows, later in firearms and cannon. Reshaped global warfare.

name: Astrolabe
description: Astronomical instrument measuring the altitude of celestial bodies; perfected by Islamic scholars. Essential to navigation and timekeeping.

name: Terrace Farming
description: Stepped fields cut into mountainsides with retaining walls, allowing intensive agriculture on steep slopes while preventing erosion.

name: Chinampa Agriculture
description: Artificial floating islands of mud and vegetation on lake surfaces, yielding multiple harvests per year of maize, beans, and squash.

name: Maya Long Count Calendar
description: Precise astronomical calendar tracking cycles of days across thousands of years, based on sophisticated observation of Venus and eclipses.

name: Movable Type Printing
description: Clay and later metal movable type for printing, developed by Bi Sheng. Precursor to Gutenberg's press by four centuries.

name: Archimedes Screw
description: Helical pump for lifting water, used in irrigation and mine drainage. Credited to Archimedes of Syracuse.

name: Humoral Medicine
description: Medical system based on four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile), codified by Hippocrates and Galen. Dominated Western medicine for 2000 years.

name: Aqueducts
description: Gravity-fed stone channels carrying water across long distances to cities, using precise gradients and arched bridges.
